The sales closing rate among eligible households in treatment areas was 38% compared to 6% among ineligible treatment households.
Among subsidy-qualifying households, offering subsidies increased the village-level latrine purchase rate by 32% (p ¼ 0.00).
Offering targeted subsidies signiﬁcantly increases the likelihood of a household purchasing a latrine.
The latrine sales described here refer to orders, not installations.

raw_response.headline_result_summary: In a 30-village cluster-randomized controlled trial (2,821 unique household sales presentations) in rural Kampong Chhnang province, Cambodia, offering targeted 50% price subsidies (using government IDPoor status plus Poverty Probability Index thresholds adjusted for household and community climate vulnerability) substantially and significantly increased purchases of durable/climate-resilient latrines. Being offered a subsidy increased an eligible household's predicted probability of purchasing a latrine by 31.3 percentage points relative to ineligible control households (Table 1: +0.313, p = 0.00; raw closing rate 38% among subsidy-offered treatment households vs. 6% among ineligible treatment households and 8% among unsubsidized eligible control households). At the village level, offering targeted subsidies increased the overall latrine sales closing rate by 23 percentage points (p = 0.00; 22% vs. 7% across all sales presentations) and increased the village-level purchase rate among subsidy-qualifying households by 32 percentage points (p = 0.00), including +37 percentage points among PPI-qualifying households (p = 0.00) and +26 percentage points among IDPoor households (p = 0.03). Purchase rates among ineligible households did not differ between treatment and control villages (+0.0056, p = 0.860), indicating no market distortion.
raw_response.specification_or_coding_pitfalls: 1. Percentage vs. percentage-point wording: The authors intermittently write '%' when reporting linear/marginal probability differences in percentage points (e.g., Highlights: 'by 31%', p. 6: 'by 32% (p = 0.00)' and '26% increase', whereas the Abstract and Table 1 text state '32 percentage points', '31 percentage points (0.313)', and '37 percentage points'). Coders must not misread '31%' or '32%' as relative risk increases—they are percentage-point increases (e.g., ~8% to ~38–40%). 2. Reference category in Table 1: In Table 1 (p. 6), the base category for the +0.313 marginal probability is 'Control / Not eligible', not 'Control / Eligible' (+0.0132, p = 0.416); comparing 'Treatment / Eligible' directly to 'Control / Eligible' yields roughly a 30 percentage-point difference (38% vs. 8% raw rates; 32 pp at the village level). 3. Orders vs. installations: As noted in Limitations (pp. 8–9), the outcome variable captures latrine purchase orders during sales presentations rather than verified physical installations (typical iDE order cancellation rates are 10–20% and were not tracked during the 7.5-month pilot). 4. Differential targeting across arms: Subsidy eligibility was higher in treatment villages (51–52%) than control villages (45%, p = 0.00), driven by a 5 percentage-point higher share of IDPoor households identified in treatment villages (p = 0.00) because village authorities helped sales agents locate poor households without toilets more actively when subsidies were available. 5. Supporting Information tables: Full regression tables for the village-level OLS models (e.g., Table 8) and baseline balance checks reside in the online Supporting Information rather than the main 10-page PDF, and Table 1 does not specify in its caption whether the printed marginal probabilities come from the unadjusted base logit or the climate-controlled logit described on p. 5.
raw_response.study_design: Cluster-randomized controlled trial (village-level random assignment stratified by commune climate vulnerability status) supplemented by 13 qualitative stakeholder interviews and programmatic cost-effectiveness analysis
raw_response.unit_and_sample_size: 30 rural villages (15 treatment, 15 control; 23 designated climate-vulnerable [12 treatment, 11 control]) in Kampong Chhnang province, Tonle Sap Lake region; 2,821 unique household sales presentations to households without a toilet (after dropping 1,598 duplicate follow-up visits), yielding 437 latrine orders (326 treatment, 111 control) and 2,352 non-purchasing household responses; plus 13 qualitative interviews
